# Cardiac stress testing

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Cardiology and angiology > Basics of cardiology > Cardiac stress testing*

[Original Article Link](/library/iD0JVR)

---

## Summary

Cardiac <u>stress</u> testing is an umbrella term for diagnostic studies that evaluate cardiac function using <u>ECG</u> or <u>cardiac imaging</u> while <u>stress</u> is induced in the <u>heart</u>. Imaging modalities include <u>echocardiography</u>, <u>myocardial perfusion imaging</u> (<u>MPI</u>), and <u>cardiac MRI</u> (<u>CMR</u>). Cardiac <u>stress</u> testing is most commonly used to assess for <u>stress</u>-induced cardiac <u>ischemia</u>. <u>Stress</u> is induced by increasing <u>heart rate</u> and contractility (using exercise or <u>dobutamine</u>) or inducing a <u>coronary steal phenomenon</u> (using <u>vasodilators</u> such as <u>adenosine</u>, <u>dipyridamole</u>, or <u>regadenoson</u>), which leads to increased <u>myocardial oxygen demand</u>, facilitating the detection of <u>myocardial</u> <u>ischemia</u>.

---

## Overview

### General principles




* <u>Myocardial</u> <u>stress</u> can be induced through exercise or pharmacological substances.

* Choice of testing modality depends on the indication and patient factors (including ability to exercise and contraindications). [[1]](/library/OS1I-T0)

* <u>Beta blockers</u>, <u>CCBs</u>, and <u>nitrates</u> can affect <u>stress</u> test results and may be held before testing. [[2]](/library/DtX1f-)

* End testing when: [[2]](/library/DtX1f-)[[3]](/library/3CXS7Z0)[[4]](/library/vtXA2-)

* Diagnostic <u>endpoint</u> is reached (e.g., findings suggestive of <u>stress</u>-induced <u>ischemia</u>) [[5]](/library/r8XfL-)[[6]](/library/1CX2IZ0)

* Target <u>heart rate</u> threshold is achieved (if no diagnostic <u>endpoint</u> is reached)

* Significant <u>cardiac arrhythmia</u>

* Any indications for early test termination are present (see “<u>Exercise stress testing</u>” and “<u>Pharmacological stress testing</u>” for respective indications)





> [!TIP]
> <u>Exercise stress testing</u> is generally preferred for evaluating <u>stress</u>-induced <u>ischemia</u>. [[3]](/library/3CXS7Z0)[[7]](/library/3tXSW-)




### Common uses [[2]](/library/DtX1f-)[[6]](/library/1CX2IZ0)[[8]](/library/50Xig9)




* Evaluation for <u>myocardial</u> <u>ischemia</u> in selected patients, e.g.:

* <u>Stable angina</u> or <u>anginal equivalents</u>: most useful for risk <u>stratification</u> in patients with an intermediate to high <u>pretest probability of obstructive CAD</u>  [[7]](/library/3tXSW-)

* <u>Cardiomyopathy</u> or <u>heart failure</u> of unclear etiology

* <u>CAD</u> risk assessment after <u>cardiac revascularization</u>

* <u>Valvular heart disease</u>: to determine exercise capacity [[9]](/library/-FXDk-)

* Selected <u>cardiac arrhythmias</u>: e.g., for treatment evaluation





> [!TIP]
> Cardiac <u>stress</u> testing is most commonly used to assess for <u>stress</u>-induced <u>ischemia</u>.




### Monitoring during examination [[5]](/library/r8XfL-)




* <u>Heart rate</u>

* Target <u>heart rate</u>: 85% of the <u>maximum heart rate</u>

* Estimated <u>maximum heart rate</u> = 220 - age (in years)

* Blood pressure

* 12-lead <u>ECG</u>

---

## Exercise stress testing

### Modalities [[2]](/library/DtX1f-)[[6]](/library/1CX2IZ0)[[10]](/library/QtXuW-)[[11]](/library/T-W69L0)




* Exercise ECG testing

* Exercise stress imaging

* <u>Stress echocardiography</u>

* <u>Stress CMR</u>

* <u>Stress MPI</u>





![Exercise ECG testing (stationary bicycle)](media/s3udcu7ca0aps9xkl199sh37.jpg)

Exercise ECG testing (stationary bicycle)




### Contraindications [[2]](/library/DtX1f-)[[3]](/library/3CXS7Z0)




* Inability to exercise

* Recent <u>unstable angina</u> or acute <u>MI</u> (within the past 2 days)

* Uncontrolled symptomatic and/or hemodynamically significant <u>arrhythmias</u>

* Symptomatic <u>severe aortic stenosis</u>

* Acute cardiac conditions, e.g.:

* Active <u>endocarditis</u>

* Acute <u>aortic dissection</u>

* Acute <u>myocarditis</u> or <u>pericarditis</u>

* <u>Decompensated heart failure</u>

* <u>Relative contraindications</u> include:

* Other cardiovascular conditions: e.g., <u>tachyarrhythmias</u>, <u>AV block</u>, recent <u>stroke</u> or <u>TIA</u>

* Circulation-relevant conditions: e.g., significant <u>anemia</u>, <u>electrolyte</u> imbalances

* Modality-specific restrictions (e.g., <u>contraindications to MRI</u>)





### Procedure [[2]](/library/DtX1f-)[[6]](/library/1CX2IZ0)




* Follow the standard or modified <u>Bruce protocol</u>.   [[6]](/library/1CX2IZ0)

* Induce <u>stress</u> using a treadmill or bicycle.

* Quantify exercise intensity using <u>metabolic equivalents</u>.

* Adjust exercise intensity to achieve the target <u>heart rate</u> (85% of <u>maximum heart rate</u>).

* Continue the protocol until the diagnostic <u>endpoint</u> is reached or there is an indication for early termination.





### Indications for early termination  [[3]](/library/3CXS7Z0)




* <u>Cyanosis</u>, <u>pallor</u>, <u>ataxia</u>, <u>dizziness</u>, or near-<u>syncope</u>

* Severe <u>dyspnea</u>

* Moderate to severe <u>angina</u>

* Decrease in systolic BP > 10 mm Hg below resting BP with other signs of <u>ischemia</u>

* Relative indications

* Symptoms: increasing <u>chest pain</u>, fatigue, <u>wheezing</u>, leg cramps, <u>claudication</u>

* <u>Vital signs</u>

* Decrease in systolic BP ≥ 10 mm Hg below resting BP without other signs of <u>ischemia</u>

* Exaggerated hypertensive response, i.e., systolic BP > 250 mm Hg or <u>diastolic</u> BP > 115 mm Hg

* <u>Heart rate</u> > 85% of age-predicted maximum

* <u>ECG</u>

* Excessive <u>downsloping ST depression</u> or <u>horizontal ST depression</u> of > 0.2 mV (2 mm)

* <u>Arrhythmias</u> with the potential to become hemodynamically significant

* <u>Bundle branch block</u> (if unable to distinguish from <u>ventricular tachycardia</u>)





![Indications for early termination of exercise ECG testing](media/jqwrfs4xctfy9c5to1xyrr1q.jpg)

Indications for early termination of exercise ECG testing




### Interpretation




See “<u>Diagnosis of coronary artery disease</u>” for findings suggesting <u>CAD</u>.

## Pharmacological stress testing

### Modalities [[1]](/library/OS1I-T0)[[8]](/library/50Xig9)




* <u>Stress echocardiography</u>

* <u>Stress CMR</u>

* <u>Stress MPI</u>





> [!TIP]
> <u>ECG</u> monitoring is typically used in addition to <u>cardiac imaging</u>.




### Contraindications [[1]](/library/OS1I-T0)[[4]](/library/vtXA2-)




* General restrictions

* Systolic BP > 200 mm Hg or <u>diastolic</u> BP > 110 mm Hg

* Acute <u>MI</u> within the past 2–4 days, <u>unstable angina</u>, <u>acute coronary syndrome</u>

* Substance-specific contraindications: See “Procedure” below.

* Modality-specific contraindications (e.g., <u>contraindications to MRI</u>)





### Procedure [[1]](/library/OS1I-T0)[[8]](/library/50Xig9)




<u>Stress</u> is induced by substances that simulate the effect of exercise on the <u>myocardium</u>.




#### Positive <u>inotropes</u> or <u>chronotropes</u>




* Agent: <u>dobutamine</u>

* Mechanism: increases <u>heart rate</u> and contractility

* Contraindications

* Obstructive <u>cardiomyopathy</u>

* <u>Aortic dissection</u>

* <u>Tachyarrhythmias</u>





#### <u>Vasodilators</u>




* Agents: <u>dipyridamole</u>, <u>adenosine</u>, or <u>regadenoson</u>

* Mechanism: induces a <u>coronary steal phenomenon</u>

* Contraindications

* Active <u>bronchospasm</u>, <u>reactive airway disease</u>, or history of severe <u>reactive airway disease</u>

* Systolic BP < 90 mm Hg

* <u>Adenosine</u> or <u>regadenoson</u> <u>stress</u> tests: <u>second-degree AV block</u>, <u>third-degree AV block</u>, or sinus node disease in patients without a pacemaker

* Preparation

* Hold <u>methylxanthines</u> (e.g., <u>caffeine</u>, aminophylline) for 12 hours before testing.

* Before <u>adenosine</u> or <u>regadenoson</u> <u>stress</u> tests: Hold <u>dipyridamole</u> for 48 hours.





### Indications for early termination [[4]](/library/vtXA2-)




* <u>Wheezing</u>, <u>cyanosis</u>, <u>pallor</u>

* Systolic BP < 80 mm Hg

* <u>Chest pain</u> with excessive <u>downsloping ST depression</u> or <u>horizontal ST depression</u> of > 0.2 mV (2 mm)

* Symptomatic <u>second-degree AV block</u> or <u>third-degree AV block</u>

* For <u>dobutamine</u> only:

* Exaggerated hypertensive response

* Systolic BP > 230 mm Hg

* OR <u>diastolic</u> BP > 115 mm Hg

* <u>Heart rate</u> > 85% of age-predicted maximum





### Interpretation




See “<u>Diagnosis of coronary artery disease</u>” for findings suggesting <u>CAD</u>.
